newsitem.title: UK: UK cereals farmers see little impact from cold.
newsitem.headline: UK cereals farmers see little impact from cold.

text.p: Despite cold weather and snow in some areas, UK cereals producers do not yet expect any damage to crops.
"We're not unduly worried at the moment," one farmer in East Anglia said. "Our biggest problem is having to chase hungry pigeons off the rapeseed."

East Anglia, one of the country's main cereals producing areas, is expected to bear much of the brunt of the cold and snow this week. The farmer reckoned that it would be impossible to assess the impact of the winter cold on grain until March.
With crops dormant, cold weather is not likely to make much difference to the UK's grains crop, a farming sector analyst said.
"Most crops are well established. I don't expect any effect," he said.
"It's been quite a dry winter and most farmers are happy (with the state of cereals crops)," he said.

A spokeswoman for the National Farmers Union's regional office in East Anglia said that farmers were as yet unconcerned. "Normally a covering of snow doesn't have any effect at all," she said. But prolonged snow cover, lasting a month or more could create problems. In the UK's generally temperate climate nobody expected that to happen, she said. --Christopher Lyddon, London newsroom +44 171 542 7928
